newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvian deficit-free budget passes first reading.
newsitem.headline: Latvian deficit-free budget passes first reading.

text.p: Latvia's 1997 budget, which is without a deficit, got through a first reading in parliament on Monday after five hours of debate, Latvian radio said.
The balanced budget is one the main economic planks of Prime Minister Andris Shkele and is also one of the conditions Latvia has to fulfill to obtain International Monetary Fund (IMF) credits.
A total 65 deputies out of the 100-seat parliament backed the budget at its first reading and 16 voted against, the radio said. The second and final reading is set for November 6.
The 1996 budget foresees a deficit of 40 million lats, while the 1995 deficit soared to 90 million lats.
The deficit free budget has caused some controversy as unions say state-fund workers have to suffer too much.
Members of parliament were greeted by a small demonstration as they made their way to parliament to start debating the budget.
